title: Dholavira: water held in stone
alt: Excavated stone reservoir with stepped sides at Dholavira
caption: A surviving reservoir at Dholavira, photographed 27 May 2017. The city developed over several phases; its whole-site date range does not date this individual structure.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Mohenjo-daro: the Great Bath
alt: Brick-lined Great Bath with a later Buddhist stupa in the background
caption: The Great Bath in the Harappan city; photograph 15 September 2016. The Buddhist stupa behind it belongs to the second century CE, not the Harappan phase. The photograph alone cannot establish the bath's precise rituals.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Lothal: the excavated basin
alt: Long brick-lined basin at Lothal, with water remaining in part of it
caption: Photographed 29 October 2016. The basin is interpreted as a dock in the UNESCO Tentative List submission; its function and ancient water connections require archaeological argument, not just its present appearance.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Cubical weights: a museum comparison
alt: Three cubical stone weights from Mohenjo-daro displayed at the Ashmolean
caption: Mohenjo-daro weights, about 2600-1900 BCE, Ashmolean Museum; photographed 23 August 2022. These are different objects from CSMVS accession IV 483 discussed in the account. Perspective is not a scale for comparing their masses.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Carnelian and terracotta: finished beads
alt: Red carnelian and pale terracotta tubular beads displayed together
caption: Mohenjo-daro, about 2600-1900 BCE; British Museum 1939,0619.345-346 and 1939,0619.305-308. Photographed 9 March 2020. Finished objects provide a comparison for Harappan craft production; these are not excavated debris from the Harappa workshop.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Cemetery H: a later Harappan assemblage
alt: Two decorated pottery vessels attributed to Cemetery H at Harappa
caption: Cemetery H pottery from Harappa, about 1900-1300 BCE, National Museum, New Delhi; photographed 18 November 2017. This later assemblage belongs here in the regional transition, not in the Mature Harappan cemetery at Rakhigarhi.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Painted Grey Ware from Sonkh
alt: Reassembled grey pottery bowl with dark painted lines in the Mathura museum
caption: Sonkh vessel, museum date 1000-600 BCE, Government Museum, Mathura, showcase 6-15; photographed 24 February 2013. Pottery provides material comparison with the later Vedic period, not proof of a language, textual community or epic event.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Rigveda: an early 19th-century copy
alt: Devanagari manuscript leaf with red marks and corrections
caption: Schoyen Collection MS 2097: an early 19th-century CE manuscript on paper. Its accents and corrections document a much later written witness to transmission; this is not a manuscript from the Rigveda's ancient composition period.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: A regional window on Indus farming
alt: Published map of selected archaeobotanical study sites in northwest India
caption: Bates et al., Figure 2: selected settlements used in a crop-processing study spanning about 3200-1500 BCE. This is a regional research map, not a map of all Indus cities or ancient political boundaries; the inset uses modern borders.
credit: Bates et al., Vegetation History and Archaeobotany, Figure 2
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Reading crop-processing traces
alt: Scatterplot comparing grain-to-chaff and grain-to-weed ratios across sampled settlements and phases
caption: Bates et al., Figure 3: winter-cereal ratios compare processing evidence. MH marks Mature Harappan samples; Early Harappan, Late Harappan and PGW samples are comparisons, not all evidence from 2600-1900 BCE. Published figure retained with its original labels.
credit: Bates et al., Vegetation History and Archaeobotany, Figure 3
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Burial pottery: a measured comparison
alt: Box plots and scatterplot comparing numbers of votive pots by age at Rakhigarhi
caption: Shinde et al. (2018), Figure 9. The plots compare numbers of votive pots associated with burials, not population totals. The sampled sub-adult graves had fewer pots; the pattern alone does not identify caste or the wealth of every household.
credit: Shinde et al. (2018), PLOS ONE, Figure 9
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.

title: Chandogya Upanishad: an 1865 CE copy
alt: Sanskrit manuscript leaf in Devanagari with marginal annotations
caption: A later written witness: this copy is dated 1865 CE (1922 Vikram Samvat) in the photograph record. Photographed 24 October 2018. It illustrates manuscript transmission, not the date of the ancient work's composition or an identified passage translation.
modifications: None; downloaded original or Commons-provided resized image.
